newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha inches up, LSWR sentiment weaker.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha inches up, LSWR sentiment weaker.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices moved steady to a little higher in afternoon trade on Tuesday, with traders shifting their attention from weaker near-term trading periods to a firmer July contract, market participants said.
Bids for first-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $212.25 per tonne against offers at $213.00.
Second-half June levels were assessed at about $211.00/212.00, compared with late Monday's $210.00/211.00.
In inter-month spreads, the first-half June contract's contango to first-half July was discussed at $2.00. First-half July/first-half August was quoted at around plus $2.00.
Buyers of Saudi Aramco's term naphtha cargoes were waiting for the supplier to announce the schedule for face-to-face talks to exchange views on market trends.
Aramco closed bidding for the second half of 1997 on April 4. The bids are valid until May 21.
Some traders said the negotiations are expected to take place later this month or early next month in Singapore.

Low sulphur waxy residue sentiment weakened due to the closure of a hydrocracker at Indonesia's Dumai plant after a fire on Friday. Bids were heard at the formula flat to a slight discount per barrel against offers at a 30 cent premium.
